<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:transplant}
For all $u,v \in W^{1,2}(\mathbb{S}^2)$,
\begin{align}
  \int_M u\,v \,dA_M &= b_w(u, v), \label{eq:L2id}\\
  \int_M \nabla_M u \cdot_{\bar g} \nabla_M v \,dA_M &= a(u, v),
  \label{eq:dirid}
\end{align}
and $E^{-1}\lVert u \rVert_{L^2(\mathbb{S}^2)} \le \lVert u \rVert_{L^{2}_{w}} \le E\,
\lVert u \rVert_{L^2(\mathbb{S}^2)}$. In particular $W^{1,2}(M) = W^{1,2}(\mathbb{S}^2)$
with equivalent norms.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
\eqref{eq:L2id} is the first identity of \eqref{eq:conformal}. For
\eqref{eq:dirid}, $\bar g(\nabla_M u, \nabla_M v) = e^{-2\lambda}\,
\nabla u \cdot \nabla v$ pointwise by the second identity; multiplying
by $dA_M = e^{2\lambda}\,dA$ the factors cancel. This cancellation is
the conformal invariance of the Dirichlet energy, special to dimension
two. The norm comparison is $e^{-2\Lambda_0} \le w \le e^{2\Lambda_0}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:rates}
Let $w \in C^\infty(\mathbb{S}^2)$ with $0 < w_{\min} \le w \le w_{\max}$,
let (A1) and (A2) hold, and let $u \in W^{d+1,2}(\mathbb{S}^2)$ solve
\eqref{eq:poissonM}. Then the solution $u_h$ of
\eqref{eq:poissonh} satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H1rate}
  \lvert u - u_h \rvert_{1,2,M} \le C\, \lvert \triangle \rvert^{\,d}\,
  \lvert u \rvert_{d+1,2,\mathbb{S}^2},
  \qquad
  \lVert u - u_h \rVert_{L^2(M)} \le C\, \lvert \triangle \rvert^{\,d+1}\,
  \lvert u \rvert_{d+1,2,\mathbb{S}^2},
\end{equation}
with $C$ depending on $d$, $\theta_\triangle$, $w_{\min}$, $w_{\max}$ and
$\lVert w \rVert_{C^1(\mathbb{S}^2)}$. For the eigenproblem \eqref{eq:evph}, if
$\mu$ is an eigenvalue of \eqref{eq:evpM} with eigenspace
$E \subset W^{d+1,2}(\mathbb{S}^2)$, then the discrete
eigenvalues converging to $\mu$ satisfy $0 \le \mu_h - \mu \le C
\lvert \triangle \rvert^{\,2d}$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The energy estimate is C\'ea's lemma \cite[Ch.~2]{BrennerScott08} on
the $w$-mean-zero subspace, where $a$ is coercive by
Proposition~\ref{prop:exact}, with \eqref{eq:approxM} and
\eqref{eq:dirid}. For the $L^2$ estimate let $e = u - u_h$ made
$w$-mean-free and let $z$ solve $-\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^2} z = w e$,
$b_w(z,1)=0$; elliptic regularity on the closed manifold $\mathbb{S}^2$
\cite[Ch.~5]{Taylor11} gives $\lVert z \rVert_{W^{2,2}} \le C w_{\max}
\lVert e \rVert_{L^2}$. Galerkin orthogonality gives $b_w(e,e) = a(z - z_h,
e)$ for every $z_h \in S_h$, \eqref{eq:jackson} with $m = 1$ bounds
$\inf_{z_h}\lvert z - z_h \rvert_{1,2}$ by $C\lvert \triangle \rvert\lVert z \rVert_{W^{2,2}}$,
and dividing by $\lVert e \rVert_{L^{2}_{w}} \ge w_{\min}^{1/2}\lVert e \rVert_{L^2}$
and using the energy estimate gives the $L^2$ rate in the weighted
norm, which is the $L^2(M)$ norm by \eqref{eq:L2id}. The eigenvalue statement is the
Babu\v{s}ka--Osborn estimate for conforming approximation of a
symmetric pencil with compact solution operator
\cite[Sec.~7]{BabuskaOsborn91}: the eigenvalue error is bounded by the
square of the best energy approximation of the eigenspace, which
\eqref{eq:approxM} bounds by $\lvert \triangle \rvert^{\,d}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:exact}
$(u,\mu)$ is an eigenpair of \eqref{eq:evpM} if and only if it is an
eigenpair of \eqref{eq:evpS}, and no constant in this correspondence
depends on $\lambda$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Insert \eqref{eq:L2id} and \eqref{eq:dirid} into the weak form of
\eqref{eq:evpM}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:parity}
Let $\lambda \equiv 0$, so that $w \equiv 1$ and \eqref{eq:evph} is the
discrete eigenvalue problem of the round metric, and let $d$ be even.
Then for every even $\ell$ with $0 \le \ell \le d$, every spherical
harmonic $Y \in \mathcal Y_\ell$ is an exact discrete eigenfunction with
exact eigenvalue $\ell(\ell+1)$:
\begin{equation*}
  a(Y, v_h) = \ell(\ell+1)\, b_1(Y, v_h)
  \qquad \text{for all } v_h \in S_h ,
\end{equation*}
so the discrete spectrum contains $\ell(\ell+1)$ with multiplicity at
least $2\ell + 1$, and for $\lvert \triangle \rvert$ small enough the discrete
eigenvalue cluster converging to $\ell(\ell+1)$ has total multiplicity
exactly $2\ell+1$. The eigenvalues of odd order $\ell$ converge from
above at the rate $\lvert \triangle \rvert^{2d}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:parity} and \eqref{eq:global}, $\mathcal Y_\ell \subset
\mathcal B_d \subset S_h$ for even $\ell \le d$, and $-\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^2}
Y = \ell(\ell+1) Y$ for $Y \in \mathcal Y_\ell$
\cite[Ch.~2]{AtkinsonHan12}, so $\bigl(Y, \ell(\ell+1)\bigr)$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:evph} verbatim; the $2\ell+1$ harmonics of degree $\ell$ are
independent in $S_h$, which gives the multiplicity bound. By
\cite[Sec.~7]{BabuskaOsborn91}, for $\lvert \triangle \rvert$ small enough
exactly $2\ell+1$ discrete eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, lie
in a neighborhood of $\ell(\ell+1)$ that excludes the other eigenvalues
of the sphere, and these are the cluster.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
